excerpt: A wooden playset with a canopied upper deck, monkey bars, shaded sandbox, snack bar and an 8-foot wave slide.
description:
The Beach Front puts a raised play deck under a coloured canopy, with a ship's wheel and toy telescope on it — the props that turn a platform into whatever the afternoon requires. Below the deck sits a shaded sandbox, which is where younger siblings end up while older ones are climbing.
The climbing routes are a rock wall and a set of monkey bars, the latter being the feature children keep coming back to because it takes actual practice to cross. Swinging is handled by two belt swings and a trapeze, so three can use it at once rather than queueing.
A covered snack bar window with bench seating gives somewhere to put juice and craft projects, and the 8-foot wave slide handles the descent. Sand is not included.
highlights: Raised play deck with coloured canopy, ship's wheel and toy telescope
Monkey bars — the climbing feature that takes real practice
Rock wall climbing route to the upper deck
2 belt swings plus a trapeze, so three children swing at once
8-foot wave slide
Shaded sandbox below the deck (sand not included)
Covered snack bar window with bench seating
Wood construction with a canopy for shade on the deck

excerpt: A near 10-foot galvanised steel A-frame swing set with 2 belt swings, a trapeze and ground anchors.
description:
The Big Brutus is the metal one, and it is built for the job wooden sets struggle with: an extra-large swing zone where several children can swing hard at the same time without clipping each other.
The A-frame stands nearly 10 feet and is made from powder-coated galvanised steel throughout. Galvanising handles the rust, powder coating handles the finish, and between them the set needs almost nothing done to it season to season — the main practical difference from timber, which wants checking and treating.
Two belt swings with coated chains and a trapeze bar hang from it. Moulded feet with ground anchors keep it freestanding and secure without a concrete base. Pieces arrive pre-fabricated, pre-drilled and powder-coated.
highlights: Nearly 10 feet tall with an extra-large swing zone
Powder-coated galvanised steel throughout — low maintenance, rust resistant
Traditional angled A-frame for stability under hard swinging
2 belt swings with coated chains plus a trapeze bar
Moulded feet with ground anchors, freestanding without concrete
Room for several children to swing at once
Pre-fabricated, pre-drilled pieces for assembly
No seasonal staining or treating, unlike timber

excerpt: A large wooden playset with a bay-window clubhouse, play kitchen, spiral tube slide and 10-foot wave slide.
description:
The Bristol Point is one of the larger sets, and it earns the size with two distinct play zones rather than one big platform. Up top is a clubhouse with a wooden roof, bay windows that actually light the inside, two balconies, a steering wheel and a chalkboard.
Underneath is a full play kitchen — toy stovetop, grill, sink, a battery-powered blender and plastic cookware. That is the part that holds younger children for an hour at a time while older ones use the climbing routes.
There are two slides: an enclosed spiral tube slide and a 10-foot wave slide, so descents do not become a queue. Two belt swings and a trapeze cover the swinging. A working half door with a built-in chalkboard finishes the playhouse.
highlights: Raised clubhouse with wooden roof, bay windows and two balconies
Lower play kitchen with toy stovetop, grill, sink, blender and cookware
Enclosed spiral tube slide plus a 10-foot wave slide
Working half door with built-in chalkboard
2 belt swings plus a trapeze, so three children swing at once
Steering wheel and toy telescope on the upper deck
Two separate play zones, upper and lower
Bay windows light the clubhouse interior

excerpt: A compact wooden playset for smaller yards — canopied clubhouse, snack bar bench, 8-foot wave slide.
description:
The Lakewood is the one designed around a smaller garden. It keeps the parts that matter — an elevated clubhouse with a coloured canopy and windows, a lower playhouse with a full front door — without the footprint of the larger sets.
A snack bar window with attached bench seating turns the lower level into a café, which in practice is where snacks and drawing happen rather than being carried back indoors.
Two belt swings and a trapeze mean three children can swing at once. The 8-foot wave slide handles the descent, and access is by a wide flat-step ladder rather than a rope or rock wall — easier for younger children and mixed age groups than a climbing route.
highlights: Sized for smaller backyards without losing the main features
Elevated clubhouse with coloured canopy roof and windows
Lower playhouse with a full front door and windows
Snack bar window with attached bench seating
2 belt swings plus a trapeze, so three children swing at once
8-foot wave slide
Wide flat-step ladder suits younger and mixed-age children
Canopy roof provides shade on the deck

excerpt: A large wooden playset with a clubhouse and separate elevated playhouse joined by a staircase, two sandboxes.
description:
The Malibu is built around a feature the other sets do not have: two elevated structures joined by a wooden staircase. A clubhouse at one end, a playhouse at the other, and a stairway between them — which turns the set into somewhere to move through rather than a single platform to sit on.
The clubhouse has a wooden roof, balcony and windows. The playhouse has saloon-style doors and a wrap-around balcony. Beneath each sits a shaded sandbox, so there are two ground-level zones as well as two raised ones.
Two belt swings and a trapeze handle the swinging, and a 10-foot wave slide the descent. Sand is not included.
highlights: Clubhouse and elevated playhouse joined by a wooden staircase
Playhouse with saloon-style doors and a wrap-around balcony
Clubhouse with wooden roof, balcony and windows
2 shaded sandboxes, one beneath each structure (sand not included)
2 belt swings plus a trapeze, so three children swing at once
10-foot wave slide
Four distinct play zones — two raised, two at ground level
Staircase makes the set somewhere to move through, not just sit

excerpt: A wooden playset with a double rock wall for two climbers, a 6-foot rope ladder and an 8-foot wave slide.
description:
The Mount McKinley is the climbing-focused set. An extra-wide rock wall carries nine holds and a rope assist, and it is wide enough for two children to climb side by side — which matters more than it sounds, because a single-file wall turns into a queue and an argument.
A second route runs up a rope ladder over six feet tall with wooden rungs, so there are two ways to the top and they demand different things: grip and balance on the rope, reach and footwork on the wall.
The raised deck sits under a coloured canopy with a steering wheel and toy telescope, and a shaded sandbox occupies the space beneath. Two belt swings and a trapeze cover the swinging, with an 8-foot wave slide down. Sand is not included.
highlights: Extra-wide rock wall with 9 holds and rope assist — two can climb together
Rope ladder over 6 feet with wooden rungs as a second route up
Two climbing routes that demand different skills
Raised deck with coloured canopy, steering wheel and toy telescope
2 belt swings plus a trapeze, so three children swing at once
8-foot wave slide
Shaded sandbox beneath the deck (sand not included)
Canopy roof provides shade on the deck

excerpt: A cabin-style wooden playset with a play kitchen, picnic table, 12-hold rock wall and 10-foot wave slide.
description:
The Shenandoah reads as a small mountain house rather than a playground frame — part cabin, part playset. The playhouse has a full front door, a side snack bar window, and a children's picnic table with attached bench seating outside it.
Inside the play kitchen there is a toy stovetop, a sink and a cordless phone, which is the sort of detail that keeps a five-year-old occupied far longer than another slide would.
Above sits a raised clubhouse with a wooden roof and windows. Climbing is by a rock wall with 12 holds — more than most sets at this size carry. Two belt swings and a trapeze handle the swinging, and the 10-foot wave slide the way down.

Play kitchen with toy stovetop, sink and cordless phone
Children's picnic table with attached bench seating
Rock climbing wall with 12 holds
Raised clubhouse with wooden roof and windows
2 belt swings plus a trapeze, so three children swing at once
10-foot wave slide
Two zones — cabin below, clubhouse above

excerpt: A large wooden playset with a bay-window clubhouse, crow's nest lookout, spiral tube slide and 10-foot wave slide.
description:
The Skyfort III is the tall one. Above the main clubhouse sits a crow's nest — a raised lookout with a toy telescope, reached separately from the deck below — which gives the set a second storey most playsets do not have.
The clubhouse itself has a wooden roof, a balcony, a covered entryway and bay windows. Beneath it is a shaded sandbox for ground-level play.
Two slides handle descents: an enclosed spiral tube slide and a 10-foot wave slide, which keeps two groups moving at once. Swinging is on two belt swings and a trapeze. Sand is not included.

Clubhouse with wooden roof, balcony, covered entryway and bay windows
Enclosed spiral tube slide plus a 10-foot wave slide
Two slides keep two groups of children moving at once
2 belt swings plus a trapeze, so three children swing at once
Shaded sandbox beneath the clubhouse (sand not included)

excerpt: A wooden playset with upper clubhouse and lower playhouse, play kitchen, web disc swing and spiral tube slide.
description:
The Tacoma Falls is two structures stacked: a clubhouse on top, a playhouse underneath, and each is set up for a different kind of play. The clubhouse above has a wooden roof and windows; the playhouse below holds a play kitchen with a toy sink, battery-powered accessories, a cookware set and dinnerware.
The swinging is where this set differs from the others: alongside two belt swings there is a web disc swing — a flat woven disc that can be sat on, stood on or lain across, and which more than one child can use at once. It tends to be the most-used part of a set that has one.
A crow's nest with a toy telescope sits above, and an enclosed spiral tube slide provides the way down.
highlights: Web disc swing — sit, stand or lie on it, and share it
2 classic belt swings alongside the disc
Upper clubhouse with wooden roof and windows
Lower playhouse with play kitchen, cookware set and dinnerware
Battery-powered kitchen accessories

excerpt: A compact wooden playset with a canopied deck, 6-hold rock wall ladder, snack bar bench and 8-foot wave slide.
description:
The Tucson is the entry point to the wooden range, and it is put together sensibly for it. The elevated deck sits under a coloured canopy that gives real shade, which turns the platform into somewhere children will actually stay on a hot afternoon.
Access is by a rock wall with six climbing holds that doubles as a ladder — so it is a climbing challenge for a confident child and an ordinary way up for one who is not, without needing two separate structures.
A covered snack bar window with bench seating sits below, and a shaded sandbox occupies the ground beneath the deck. Two belt swings and a trapeze cover the swinging, with an 8-foot wave slide down. Sand is not included.
highlights: Rock wall with 6 holds that doubles as a ladder
Works for confident climbers and cautious ones without a second route
Raised deck with coloured canopy roof for shade
Covered snack bar window with bench seating
Shaded sandbox beneath the deck (sand not included)
2 belt swings plus a trapeze, so three children swing at once
8-foot wave slide
